evidence: task/task.toml lines 20-24: [environment] build_timeout_sec=600.0, network_mode="public", cpus=2, memory_mb=4096; no docker_image and no allow_internet key anywhere in task.toml (only keys under [environment] are those four). Lines 17-38 diff-identical to the frozen template task.toml and to staged-task-contract.md lines 55-60/78. No secret literal under [environment]; the only credential reference in the file is ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}" (an env interpolation in the frozen [verifier.env] block, row 10's scope) and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="". task/environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical (cmp) to the template agent Dockerfile: node:22-bookworm-slim, pinned express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1, no ENV/ARG carrying keys, CMD sleep infinity. Secret grep (sk-, api_key, token, secret, private key, AKIA) over task/environment, task.toml and solution found only the documented demo sign-in password 'password123' (environment/instructions/walls-and-retention.md:3, solution server.js:17), which is a public product fixture, not a credential. 2 CPU / 4 GB is sane for an Express+better-sqlite3 app (prebuilt binaries installed at image build). Network public is correct per the current workbook 'Quality Checks' row 10; the 'Internal Quality Checks' row 10 'no-network' wording is the historical annotation superseded by the current sheet and lead guidance, so not flagged. Adversarial: no plausible broken app or conforming alternative is affected by this row since it concerns only the agent sandbox config; an agent needing extra npm packages can fetch them on the public network. Limitation: no cold build of this exact environment was measured for this round (raw-evidence-index cites agent image cw-editor-agent-r3), but the Dockerfile is byte-equal to the template, so no new build risk is introduced.
